title: Secretary Scott Bessent's Statement Before the Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government
summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent testified before the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on FY2027 budget, requesting a 12% decrease from the enacted level while highlighting the administration's signature tax relief policies and IRS modernization efforts. The testimony noted over 60 million tax returns claimed at least one Trump tax cut and referenced the GENIUS Act as landmark legislation creating the first regulatory framework for stablecoins.
key_points: FY2027 Treasury budget request represents a 12% decrease from enacted level while maintaining core financial operations

Over 60 million tax returns claimed at least one of President Trump's new tax cuts during filing season; 7 million filers claimed No Tax on Tips (avg $7,000+), 28 million claimed No Tax on Overtime (avg $3,100+)
34 million seniors claimed Enhanced Deduction for Seniors with average deduction over $7,500
Nearly 5.5 million Trump Accounts opened with 1.3 million children eligible for $1,000 pilot contribution
GENIUS Act identified as 'landmark legislation that created the first-ever regulatory framework for stablecoins'
Budget prioritizes national security through cyber capabilities, sanctions enforcement, and combating illicit financial activity
